llm.summary: The skill is a coherent bid-analysis assistant, but it needs review because it can collect a hashed device identifier, persist an API key, and export shareable reports containing login-bypass signed links.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the vendor API are proportionate for the skill, and local tender-file reads are user-directed, but MAC-derived device fingerprinting and default local report files containing signed links are higher impact than the analysis task requires.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer or package-install step was found. The manifest declares ZLBX_API_KEY, but runtime instructions also use ~/.zlbx/config.json and an executable local report-rendering script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses most sensitive steps and requires user consent before auto-registration, but complete-mode HTML export is default behavior and the instructions require raw signed URLs in chat and exported reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes API credentials to ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes persistent HTML reports under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files; those reports can include signed access URLs with no documented expiration or redaction.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core API-based bid analysis, user-provided tender-file parsing, and report generation fit the stated purpose, but automatic account provisioning and mandatory preservation of signed sk login-bypass URLs expand the capability beyond ordinary analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the vendor API workflow: the skill may create a trial account after consent, send a hashed MAC-derived device identifier for trial de-duplication, store an API key locally, and write reports to your home directory. Treat generated HTML reports and copied links as sensitive because they may contain signed access parameters; avoid sharing them outside the intended audience.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local reads of user-provided tender files and report writes are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the artifact does not fully declare config-file credential storage and report persistence in metadata.
[TP4] expected: HTML report generation is aligned with producing a bid-analysis report, but the default shareable artifact includes platform branding and may embed signed access links.
[SDI-2] expected: Account bootstrap and API-key persistence support zero-configuration API access and are consent-gated, but they materially broaden credential handling for an analysis skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The auto-registration reference instructs collection of platform, CPU architecture, and a MAC-derived hash for trial de-duplication; this is disclosed, but not necessary for the core bid-analysis function.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The MAC-derived hash is a persistent device identifier even though the raw MAC is not sent; the artifact frames it as trial abuse prevention rather than analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The report template requires preserving sk parameters in output links; because the artifact describes sk as an免登录 signature, raw redistribution is not required for analytical conclusions.
[SDI-1] expected: Running a local Python renderer and writing an HTML report is consistent with report export, but making it default in full mode increases persistent local side effects.
[SQP-2] expected: The report path is documented, but full-mode export happens by default after the chat report rather than as an explicit export request.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The artifact-backed concern is valid: sk is explicitly described as a login-bypass signature and is required to be preserved in chat, citations, and exported HTML.
